title: When the Provision Falls
premise: Rosalind Eriksen chases storms for hire across a monsoon-battered coast, owing debts to the Meridian Syndicate—optimists who lend money and collect in blood. When a government survey team vanishes near the drowned delta, leaving intact gear and no tracks, the Syndicate forces him to salvage it as payment. With a stranger named Ilsa Vane whose motives shift like weather, he discovers the team found something worth killing for: proof that the government engineered the floods to seize land. Outlasting the monsoon in a leaking boat, hunted by both the Syndicate and the survey's true owners, Rosalind must choose between selling the evidence to clear his debt or exposing it and losing everything. He chooses truth, survives the dry season's first dawn, and walks away owning nothing but his name.
about_author: Casper Thornbury is the pen name of a former marine surveyor who spent six seasons charting flood zones before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels from a houseboat that has sunk twice.

chapters.title: Debt Weather
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A storm-chasing contract goes wrong when lightning destroys his sensor rig; the Meridian Syndicate's collector, Brann, arrives with a smile and a ledger. The emotional beat is dread disguised as charm—we learn Rosalind keeps moving because stopping means settling accounts he can't pay.

chapters.title: The Vanishing at Saltmere Delta
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. News breaks: a nine-person government survey team vanished overnight near the delta, gear untouched, no tracks in the mud. The Syndicate offers to forgive his debt if he salvages their equipment. Beat: temptation wearing a fair face; Rosalind accepts against his instincts.

chapters.title: Leaking Hull, Rising Water
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He buys the only boat available—a rotting skiff named Patience—and pushes into the delta as the monsoon's second wave builds. Beat: grim humor and mounting unease as the landscape shows signs someone left in a hurry, or was taken.

chapters.title: The Stranger on the Sandbar
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He finds Ilsa Vane stranded on a sandbar with a broken radio and a survey-team jacket that isn't hers. She claims to be a journalist. Beat: wary alliance; two liars recognizing each other and agreeing not to ask questions yet.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. They reach the abandoned camp: generators still running, meals half-eaten, every map and data drive removed except one hidden case Ilsa seems too eager to find. Beat: creeping horror—the team didn't flee; they were collected.

chapters.title: What the Floods Were For
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Her POV reveals she was the team's communications officer who slipped away before the abduction. The hidden case holds evidence the government's water authority deliberately breached levees to depopulate and seize delta land. Beat: righteous fury colliding with her guilt over abandoning her crew.

chapters.title: Brann's Second Smile
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The Syndicate's collector catches up by airboat, expecting salvage, not witnesses. Rosalind hides the case and lies badly. Beat: terror under pressure—he realizes the Syndicate isn't just collecting debt; they're brokering the evidence for the government.

chapters.title: Running the Drowned Forest
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A chase through submerged timber as Brann's boats hunt them. The Patience takes hull damage; they escape by luring pursuers into a collapsing deadfall. Beat: adrenaline and the first flicker of trust—Ilsa saves his life without hesitation.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Dry Hold
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Bailing water through the night, they trade truths: her desertion, his debt, the names of the missing team. Beat: intimacy forged by shared danger; both admit they're each planning to betray the other if it comes to it.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold the Rain
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. They track the operation's local architect, water official Aldous Renk, to a fortified station upriver. Beat: cold clarity—Rosalind sees how cheaply lives were priced, and recognizes his own debt-ledger logic mirrored in the villains.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Ruin
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. She reveals the flooded land was her family's; the survey team included her brother. Her search was never journalism—it was inheritance, reclaiming what the water took. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose; the theme of inheritance made personal.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Optimists
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind secretly contacts the Syndicate offering the case for full debt forgiveness. Brann agrees—but Ilsa overhears. Beat: self-loathing and betrayal; loyalty vs. truth turns inward as he nearly sells the story to buy his own skin.

chapters.title: Monsoon's Worst Hour
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The season's peak storm hits while they're mid-river; the Patience begins to sink. Ilsa refuses to help bail until he explains himself. Beat: raw confrontation inside life-threatening chaos—truth extracted by rising water.

chapters.title: What Stopping Costs
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Wrecked on a shoal, they shelter with delta holdouts who lost everything to the engineered floods. Their stories strip away Rosalind's excuses. Beat: moral reckoning; he understands why stopping—facing what he owes beyond money—costs more than moving ever did.

chapters.title: Renk's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Infiltrating Renk's station, they find the mirror document: the government's own accounting of the operation, complete with the Syndicate as middlemen. Beat: cold triumph curdling—clearing his debt would make him a line in that same ledger.

chapters.title: The Case Changes Hands
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Brann ambushes them at the exchange point; Ilsa surrenders herself to buy Rosalind time, taking the real case with her. Beat: sacrifice and reversal—she bets everything that he'll choose truth over freedom.

chapters.title: Dry Season Deadline
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Waters recede; the delta becomes passable, meaning the government can move the remaining witnesses. Rosalind repairs the Patience with holdout help and races the calendar. Beat: desperate resolve—he stops running and starts choosing.

chapters.title: Storm Chaser's Gambit
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He deliberately sails into the last storm cell of the season, using its chaos to breach Renk's station where Ilsa is held. Beat: audacity born of desperation; the skills that kept him alive become weapons for someone other than himself.

chapters.title: The Price Collected
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Escape through flooding corridors; Brann dies in the collapse he caused chasing them, and Renk flees with nothing. Ilsa is wounded. Beat: costly victory—the price of survival paid in blood, not coin, and Rosalind carries her out.

chapters.title: Broadcast Before the Calm
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Using the station's transmitter before authorities seal the zone, they broadcast the evidence wide enough that burying it costs more than admitting it. Beat: catharsis—truth released can't be repossessed, and neither can the consequences.

chapters.title: Settling Accounts
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Investigations begin; the Syndicate disavows Brann and voids Rosalind's debt to erase their trail—freedom bought by scandal, not payment. Ilsa recovers and claims her family's land back from the water. Beat: bittersweet justice; debts dissolved but never truly forgiven.

chapters.title: First Light, Dry Ground
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. On the first clear dawn of the dry season, Rosalind stands on reclaimed delta ground with nothing—no debt, no rig, no boat worth the name—and finds he can finally stop moving. Beat: quiet resolution; survival's price was everything, and it was worth it.
